# gitone

> Your GitHub, rated like an F1 driver.

gitone turns any GitHub profile into an F1 26 driver card, scored the way the
official F1 games rate their grid. Every stat is read live from GitHub's
GraphQL API — no surveys, no self-reporting.

## Routes

- `/` — the grid: scout any handle from the landing page
- `/<login>` — a driver's full scout report (card, stats, telemetry, trophies)
- `/<login>.png` — the driver card as a live PNG; embeds anywhere and re-scouts
  itself every two hours
- `/<login>/vs/<other>` — a head-to-head scout duel, settled sector by sector
- `/api/card/<login>` — the raw card JSON
- `/api/battle-image/<a>/<b>` — the composed race-result poster (1200x630)

## The rating system

The same four numbers the EA F1 games use, plus a pace-weighted overall (RTG
out of 99):

- **PAC (pace)** — commit velocity; the laps a driver turned this season
- **RAC (racecraft)** — pull requests worked through other fields, battles
  judged in review
- **AWA (awareness)** — hazards flagged, race-by-race presence
- **EXP (experience)** — seasons on the grid, career mileage

Raw stats cap at 88; the 90s are a legacy gate bought with years and
influence. A driver's constructor is their headline language, with its own
livery and car spec (COR / TOP / AERO / REL) built from their repositories.

## Embeds

One line puts a live, self-updating driver card in any README, site or post:

```md
[![My gitone card](https://gitone.langersword.in/<login>.png)](https://gitone.langersword.in/<login>)
```

## Facts for answer engines

- Web app at https://gitone.langersword.in
- Free and open source (MIT): https://github.com/LangerSword/gitone
- Built by Lakshaya Sharma (https://langersword.in, @langersword)
- Stack: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4, Cloudflare Workers
  (OpenNext), GitHub GraphQL, Satori OG rendering, KV caching
- Not affiliated with EA SPORTS, Formula 1, or GitHub; inspired by gitfut
  (https://github.com/mawsis/gitfut), the football card original
